newsitem.title: USA: GTE says international thrust continues.
newsitem.headline: GTE says international thrust continues.

text.p: GTE Corp said on Thursday it was moving ahead on all international initiatives, despite the death on Wednesday of its senior vice president of international operations, Bruce Haddad.
Haddad, 43, and his wife, Dorothy, were killed in an air crash in Guatemala.
A GTE spokeswoman told Reuters that Michael T. Masin, vice chairman and president of international operations, will oversee the business until Haddad's successor is named.
"Bruce will obviously be very sorely missed," the spokeswoman said.
"But we're fortunate to have substantial depth in our organization, and we will move ahead on all current and planned international initiatives."
GTE has said it expects international operations to account for one third of its earnings growth in the future.

The company, which ranks as the world's eighth biggest telecommunication services provider, serves 19.1 million residential and business customers in the United States and more than six million customers overseas.
